correctness.rationale: Direct structure constants give a surjective 6-to-3 bracket and kernel (a,b,c,c,-b,a); the Plücker Pfaffian on this kernel is a^2+b^2+c^2 in every field. Every annihilating bilinear form is alternating and kills the three-dimensional center in each argument, so quotienting by bracket-factorizing forms has dimension 3 minus the span rank of isotropic vectors. For nondegenerate odd-characteristic ternary forms an isotropic line admits a hyperbolic mate and an orthogonal third vector, producing three independent zeros; anisotropic gives none. In characteristic two the zero set is exactly the two-plane a+b+c=0. Projective scheme and finite-field count follow as written; five-field direct exact checker confirms all finite cases without substituting for proof.

value.rationale: The same natural fixed integral 7-dimensional class-two Lie bracket has ZPD defect 3 over R/Q, 0 over C and finite odd fields, and 1 in characteristic two, giving a meaningful exact field-sensitive structural boundary. The projective commuting-plane conic smooth-to-double-line degeneration explains the difference, while the uniform finite-field pair census shows a natural numerical invariant misses that obstruction. This is a motivated interaction of Lie-algebra structure, arithmetic and incidence geometry; no claim of novel general ZPD criterion.
